# SB-1040: Safety bulletin: arc flash at the induction power cabinet

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-SB01

Hazard description
The induction power cabinet serving the Ring Rolling line exhibited an intermittent flash event during maintenance access. The flash hazard results from stored energy in the cabinet buswork and capacitors, and from inadvertent energization while covers are removed. Personnel entering the cabinet or working adjacent to exposed conductors are at risk of arc flash injury, burns, and secondary hazards from startle or falls. The condition is compounded by particulate accumulation in the shot blast area which can create conductive pathways if media migrates into electrical enclosures.

Affected equipment
Primary affected asset: EQ-P3-L2-SB01 (Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1) and the adjacent induction power cabinet. Associated controls and procedures used on this line include MM-P3-L2-SB01, SOP-P3-L2-02, and SOP-P3-L2-04.

Required controls
- De-energize and lockout-tagout the induction power cabinet before removing any covers; verify zero energy per SOP-P3-L2-02.  
- Perform a visual and vacuum clean of accessible external cabinet surfaces and surrounding floor prior to cover removal; remove shot media build-up that could enter enclosures in accordance with MM-P3-L2-SB01. The shot media top-up interval for Ring Rolling shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L2-SB01) is 40 hours.  
- Use insulated tools and maintain a minimum approach distance consistent with SOP-P3-L2-04 when working on or near live parts if any work is authorized live. Live work is not authorized unless specifically approved by maintenance leadership and electrical engineering per SOP-P3-L2-04.  
- Personnel must wear arc-rated protection as required by site PPE lists and remain trained on energized work authorization procedures in MM-P3-L2-SB01.

Effective date
This bulletin is effective upon release of Revision Rev E and applies to all work on P3-L2 until superseded.
